pretexts: concert or event tickets for high-demand sold-out events
rental properties in ideal locations at low prices
buyer offers to pay above asking price to cover shipping
buyer requests VIN report for vehicle history
buyer claims to send e-Transfer but sends payment request instead
interac_context: Fraudsters claim to send an e-Transfer to pay for an item, but actually send a request for funds from the victim's account or a phishing message asking for banking credentials.
emerging_tactics: QR codes asking to confirm banking information
compromised social media accounts to impersonate friends
phishing links for VIN reports that steal credit card information
e-Transfer payment requests disguised as payments

kill_chain_signals.contact: Fraudsters contact via social media, classified websites, or impersonate compromised friends; post fake ads on social media and paid ads
kill_chain_signals.pretext: Urgent payment for high-demand tickets, low-price rentals, drastic discounts, overpayment offers, VIN report requests, fake e-Transfer claims
kill_chain_signals.payment: Request immediate payment via e-Transfer, credit card for fake VIN reports, fake payment notifications asking for tracking numbers, counterfeit cheques
kill_chain_signals.movement: Seller asked to ship product and provide tracking number before payment is released; funds transferred for shipping fees
kill_chain_signals.cashout: Credit card information used for fraudulent purchases or transactions; seller loses product and receives no payment

red_flags: Blowout sales or greatly reduced prices (e.g. 80%)
Buyers who want to buy without seeing the product first
Overpayments for items you are selling
Requests asking for money to cover shipping fees
QR codes asking to confirm your banking information
key_quote: Fraudsters will claim that they are sending an e-transfer to pay for the item, but in reality, it's a request for funds from your account.
title: Protecting yourself online
